entities.name: Boc deprotection
observations: SELFIES decoding shows conversion of R-CH2-NH-C(=O)-O-C(CH3)3 to R-CH2-NH2 with the complex heteroaromatic scaffold otherwise unchanged.
The supplied reaction is consistent with acid-mediated tert-butoxycarbonyl cleavage.

entities.name: TFA in dichloromethane
observations: Typical Boc-cleavage system: approximately 20–50% trifluoroacetic acid in dichloromethane, 0 °C to room temperature, about 0.5–2 hours.
Usually affords the amine as its trifluoroacetate salt unless basified.

entities.name: HCl in dioxane
observations: Typical alternative Boc-cleavage system: commercial HCl in dioxane, often about 4 M and approximately 1–4 equivalents, at room temperature for about 0.5–3 hours.

entities.name: HCl in ethyl acetate
observations: Operational alternative to HCl in dioxane for Boc removal; generally performed at room temperature and gives the amine hydrochloride.

entities.name: Lewis-acid Boc cleavage
observations: TMSI, BBr3, or ZnBr2 can be considered specialized alternatives, but they are less routine and may affect other heteroatoms or acid-sensitive groups.
